rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~96% (CME FedWatch via Hercules); BoJ Dec ~85% (Kalshi); BoC Dec ~80% (Reuters); BoE Dec ~82%; ECB Dec ~90%; RBA Dec hold ~99%
rows.read: A December Fed hike stays all but certain, and nothing overnight changed that. In Japan, a Bank of Japan board member hinted at faster hikes, backing a December move. Canada's central bank also looks set to hike again, which narrows the US dollar's rate edge over the loonie.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US Q3 GDP +4.3% annualized, second estimate (fcst 3.5%); Australia Q3 private capex +12.2% q/q (fcst 4.5%); Germany Q3 GDP +0.1% q/q final
rows.read: The US economy is still running hot, and Australian firms stepped up investment far more than expected. Germany barely grew over the summer. Strong growth backs higher rates in the US and Australia, while Europe lags.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US core PCE Oct +3.3% y/y (fcst 3.2%); Australia CPI Oct 4.9% y/y; Tokyo core CPI Nov due 5:30 PM CT Thu (fcst 3.0%, Oct 2.6%)
rows.read: US core inflation edged up again in October, and Australian inflation is climbing. In Japan, a rate-setter said a weak yen and costly raw materials are pushing prices up. All three keep their central banks leaning against easing.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: S&P 500 fund ~−0.3%, Nasdaq-100 fund ~−0.7% at Wed close after −4% intraday; Nikkei +1.6%, Kospi +1.9%; USD/CHF ~0.832; AUD/USD ~0.664
rows.read: US shares won back most of Wednesday's deep fall, and Asian shares bounced overnight. That cooled the rush into safe havens, so the franc gave back some gains and the Aussie recovered. Thin holiday trading can still make moves jumpy.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$94.87, WTI ~$84.10 (indicative); Brent Wed settlement $94.61 (+3.5%); OPEC+ meets Sun Nov 29
rows.read: Oil held its jump as Iran claimed another tanker hit a mine near Hormuz. That keeps helping the Canadian dollar and costs oil importers like Japan and the euro area. No claim has yet shown a real loss of supply.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Heavy bets against the loonie leave room for a fast unwind if Canadian hike bets keep growing.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies: up to 15% EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland; up to 20% extra China; 25% India; 35% Vietnam; comments due Jan 5, hearings Jan 25 (USTR); S&P France review Fri Nov 27
rows.read: The US plans new tariffs on 14 economies, hardest on China and Southeast Asia, but nothing takes effect before early 2027. France's debts remain a weight on the euro, with S&P due to review its credit rating on Friday.
